visualReview.notes: Inspected the raised fired-clay gallery envelope, alternating support geometry, southwest porch and central lower glazing, four recessed upper window banks, two connected lower wings, all eight roof lanterns and projecting drains. Verified the current connected wing geometry and exterior grade views.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected four oblique views, overhead placement, roof and wing detail, the southwest apron and northwest glazing. The terracotta, boardformed concrete, painted metal and glazing hold their hierarchy. Geographic preview fixture unloaded successfully.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 25 renders at four detail levels and two lighting conditions. Source mesh probes confirm eight separate continuous roof lanterns and coverage of both attached wing projections at each level.

geographicReview.notes: The 14 native perimeter points identify the main museum, with the two attached low projections and the separate Architecture Museum outside the site mask. The original elevation was frozen before geometry and viewed independently without cutout. The live placement comparison used a flat geographic viewer fixture, with plaza and building contacts approximated from the original field.

fidelityReview.scope: The standing main Government Museum and Art Gallery in Chandigarh’s Sector 10-C, with its attached perimeter projections, raised gallery block, southwest portico and eight roof lanterns.
fidelityReview.notes: Written architectural sources, the owner and on-site conservation researchers, support the raised exterior, alternation of round pilotis and piers, shaded southwest portico, fired-clay cladding, recessed window walls, narrow exterior aerators, eight concrete lanterns and their drainage. The specific height, glazing placement, small profiles and finishes remain estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Reviewed the published Qualla set first. The sole cleared original depicts a collection object. Neither it nor the attribution-licensed architectural photographs inform the model. Used the named native footprint, original elevation and written facts from the museum and its conservation team.

primaryFactsReview.notes: Verified the native whole-building outline and the primary written records for the pilotis, recessed glazing, fired-clay walls and eight roof lanterns. Vertical sections, bay alignment and localized finish are estimates.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Standing Government Museum and Art Gallery in Chandigarh, including both main attachments, the southwest entry portico and all eight roof lanterns.

limitations: The contemporary, named outline sets the main gallery and the two connected lower projections. The Architecture Museum is a separate nearby building. The modeled exterior covers the main museum, its raised massing, open portico and roof daylighting.

The eight roof lanterns, terracotta-facing surfaces, recessed undulatory windows and alternating round pilotis and piers follow the written museum and conservation accounts. Their vertical dimensions, component placement, fins, scuppers, glazing divisions and contemporary finish are estimates.
The preserved open terrain grid establishes the plaza-side approach. Raised ground floor, ramps, changes in grade and lower rear masses are approximate.
